```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5,
                      fig.align = "center")
```

This vignette shows how to drive `dbpmr` **cell by cell over a region**, forced by
FishMIP Earth System Model (ESM) inputs. The worked example is the **Kerguelen
Plateau** (a sub-Antarctic FishMIP regional-model domain in the Indian sector of
the Southern Ocean). Each 1° cell runs an independent coupled benthic–pelagic
size-spectrum model driven by its own local plankton spectrum and temperature.

To keep the example self-contained and laptop-friendly it is **unfished**: it maps
the equilibrium biomass the ESM forcing supports, with no fishing or calibration.
Adding fishing effort and calibrating catchability is a further step — see
*Going further* at the end.

## 1. Where the inputs come from

Two ingredients define a regional run:

* **The region boundary.** FishMIP publishes a shapefile of all regional-model
  domains at [Fish-MIP/FishMIP_regions](https://github.com/Fish-MIP/FishMIP_regions)
  (`outputs/FishMIP_regional_models.zip`). We used the **"Kerguelen Mizer"**
  polygon and kept the 1° cell centres inside it — **84 cells**.
* **The ESM forcing.** Per-region gridded forcing (temperature, phytoplankton
  carbon, export, …) can be downloaded from the
  [FishMIP Regional Climate Forcing Data Explorer](https://fishmip.global-ecosystem-model.cloud.edu.au/shiny/FishMIP_Input_Explorer/)
  (gridded `.zarr` for 3-D variables, tabular `.parquet` for summaries), or taken
  directly from the ISIMIP3a GFDL-MOM6-COBALT2 obsclim outputs.

From those raw fields we derive, **per cell and per month**, the two things the
engine needs as plankton forcing — the size-spectrum **intercept** and **slope** —
plus the **experienced** (vertically biomass-weighted) water-column temperature,
the sea-floor temperature, and the export ratio. That processing is summarised
below (not run here; it needs the full ESM netCDFs) and is described in full in
the package's gridded workflow:

```{r eval = FALSE}
# Sketch of the offline forcing build (per cell, per month), from the ESM fields:
#   intercept, slope <- GetPPIntSlope(<phyc>, <phypico>)   # <.> = vertical biomass-weighted mean, 0-200 m
#   texp             <- <thetao>                            # phyc-weighted experienced temperature
#   tob              <- sea-floor temperature
#   export           <- expc-bot / intpp
# The result is one row per (cell, year, month) — exactly what we bundle below.
```

The processed forcing for Kerguelen ships with the package so this vignette runs
without any downloads.

## 2. Load the bundled example inputs

```{r}
library(dbpmr)

ex     <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "dbpmr")
cells  <- read.csv(ex("kerguelen_cells.csv"))                 # lon, lat, depth (m)
forc   <- readRDS(ex("kerguelen_forcing.rds"))                # per cell x month forcing
params <- jsonlite::fromJSON(ex("kerguelen_biology_params.json"))$params  # global biology constants

nrow(cells)                                                   # 84 cells
range(forc$year)                                              # 1961-2010, monthly
head(forc, 3)
```

Each cell's forcing is a monthly series; we reshape it into `months × cells`
matrices for convenient indexing.

```{r}
ckey <- paste(round(forc$lon), round(forc$lat))
cid  <- match(paste(round(cells$lon), round(cells$lat)), unique(ckey))
nmo  <- nrow(forc) / nrow(cells)
mat  <- function(v) matrix(forc[[v]], nmo, nrow(cells))
Pint <- mat("intercept"); Pslp <- mat("slope"); Ptex <- mat("texp")
Ptob <- mat("tob");       Pexp <- mat("export")
yr1  <- 1:12                                                   # first-year month columns
```

## 3. A single-cell run

The helper below runs **one cell**, unfished, for `nyr` years, driven by that
cell's 12 monthly forcing values. It is a thin wrapper around the standard
`Setup.*` → `SizeSpectrum()` calls: a plankton spectrum whose intercept/slope come
from the forcing (`ts_flag = TRUE`), a temperature/`export` forcing table, and one
pelagic + one benthic size class. Passing a `state` warm-restarts from a previous
year.

```{r}
LN10 <- log(10)
imm  <- 0.15                             # recruitment floor (imm_frac of the pelagic species)
ascl <- 1/3; mu0s <- 0.5                 # search-volume scaling A/3, natural-mortality scaling
dh <- params$defecate_prop; dl <- params$def_low
Kp <- (1-dh)*params$growth_pred; Rp <- (1-dh)*(1-(params$growth_pred+params$energy_pred)); Ep <- (1-dh)*params$energy_pred
Kl <- (1-dl)*params$growth_detritivore; Rl <- (1-dl)*(1-(params$growth_detritivore+params$energy_detritivore)); El <- (1-dl)*params$energy_detritivore
te <- function(T) exp(params$c1 - params$activation_energy/(params$boltzmann*(T+273)))

run_cell <- function(depth, cint, cslp, ctex, ctob, cexp, nyr, state = NULL) {
  wd <- tempfile("cell"); dir.create(wd); old <- setwd(wd)
  on.exit({ setwd(old); unlink(wd, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE) }, add = TRUE)
  dcorr <- min(depth, 200); prefben <- 0.8 * exp(-depth/1500)
  mon   <- function(t) (floor(t*12) %% 12) + 1
  plfun <- function(m, t, x, y) { j <- mon(t); (10^cint[j]/LN10) * exp(cslp[j]*m) }
  run  <- Setup.Run("R", 1, 1, 0, TRUE, 1)
  grid <- Setup.Grid(run, tmax = nyr, tstep = 1/48, toutstep = 1)
  pl   <- Setup.Plankton(run, filename = "plankton", lambda = cslp[1], ts_flag = TRUE)
  Setup.ts(pl, run, grid, func = plfun)
  pe <- Setup.Pelagic(run, filename = "fish", mmin = -3*LN10, mmat = 2*LN10, mmax = 6*LN10,
                      alpha = params$metabolic_req_pred, A = 64*ascl, mu_0 = params$natural_mort*mu0s,
                      pref_ben = prefben, K_pla = Kp, R_pla = Rp, Ex_pla = Ep, K_pel = Kp, R_pel = Rp,
                      Ex_pel = Ep, K_ben = Kl, R_ben = Rl, Ex_ben = El, rep_method = 2, fishing_flag = FALSE,
                      imm_frac = imm)
  be <- Setup.Benthic(run, filename = "benthos", mmin = -3*LN10, mmat = 1*LN10, mmax = 4*LN10,
                      alpha = params$metabolic_req_detritivore, A = 6.4*ascl, mu_0 = params$natural_mort*mu0s,
                      K_det = Kl, R_det = Rl, Ex_det = El, rep_method = 2, fishing_flag = FALSE)
  de <- Setup.Detritus(run, filename = "detritus")
  din <- file.path("R", "Input"); dir.create(din, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  nst <- round(nyr/(1/48)) + 2; jm <- ((floor(seq_len(nst)*(1/48)*12)) %% 12) + 1
  writeLines(c("pel_tempeff,ben_tempeff,sinking_rate,depth",
               sprintf("%.8g,%.8g,%.8g,%.8g", te(ctex[jm]), te(ctob[jm]), pmax(cexp[jm], 0), dcorr)),
             file.path(din, "forcing_ts.txt"))
  if (!is.null(state)) { pe@initial_flag <- TRUE; be@initial_flag <- TRUE; de@initial_flag <- TRUE
    writeLines(paste(state$U, collapse = ","), file.path(din, "fish_ts.txt"))
    writeLines(paste(state$V, collapse = ","), file.path(din, "benthos_ts.txt"))
    writeLines(paste(state$W, collapse = ","), file.path(din, "detritus_ts.txt")) }
  invisible(utils::capture.output(SizeSpectrum(run, grid, pl, pe, be, de)))
  f <- Read.In("R", "fish"); b <- Read.In("R", "benthos"); d <- Read.In("R", "detritus")
  m <- f@mrange; dm <- diff(m)[1]
  U <- as.numeric(f@finaluvals[1, -(1:3)]); V <- as.numeric(b@finaluvals[1, -(1:3)]); W <- tail(as.numeric(d@biomass), 1)
  list(state = list(U = U, V = V, W = W), m = m, U = U, V = V,
       BU = sum(U*exp(m)*dm)*dcorr, BV = sum(V*exp(m)*dm)*20)   # depth-integrated pelagic / benthic biomass
}
```

Let's spin a handful of cells (a north–south transect) to equilibrium and look at
the pelagic and benthic biomass they support. Each cell runs a 25-year transient,
so (like the calibration in §5) the code is shown but not executed when the package
is checked — the region result below is the shipped output of exactly this loop:

```{r eval = FALSE}
sel <- cells[order(cells$lat), ][round(seq(1, nrow(cells), length.out = 5)), ]
demo <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(sel)), function(i) {
  co <- which(round(cells$lon) == round(sel$lon[i]) & round(cells$lat) == round(sel$lat[i]))[1]
  run_cell(cells$depth[co], Pint[yr1, co], Pslp[yr1, co], Ptex[yr1, co], Ptob[yr1, co], Pexp[yr1, co],
           nyr = 25)
})
data.frame(lon = sel$lon, lat = sel$lat, depth = round(sel$depth),
           pelagic_B = round(sapply(demo, `[[`, "BU"), 1),
           benthic_B = round(sapply(demo, `[[`, "BV"), 1))
```

Running all 84 cells and stepping them through the full 1961–2010 monthly forcing
(warm-restarting each year) is the same call in a loop — it takes a few minutes on
a laptop. We ship the finished output so the maps below render instantly.

## 4. Region result

```{r fig.height = 4}
res <- readRDS(ex("kerguelen_run_result.rds"))
ce  <- res$cells

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
draw <- function(z, ttl) {
  pal <- hcl.colors(64, "YlGnBu", rev = TRUE)
  plot(ce$lon, ce$lat, pch = 15, cex = 2.2, col = pal[as.integer(cut(z, 64))],
       xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude", main = ttl)
  points(c(69.2, 73.5), c(-49.3, -53.1), pch = 17)            # Kerguelen & Heard Is.
}
draw(ce$BU_recent, "Pelagic biomass")
draw(ce$BV_recent, "Benthic biomass")
```

Pelagic biomass peaks over the **northern plateau** near the islands — where the
ESM forcing carries the most phytoplankton — and declines into the colder, less
productive south.

```{r fig.height = 4}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
matplot(res$yrs, cbind(colMeans(res$BU, na.rm = TRUE), colMeans(res$BV, na.rm = TRUE)),
        type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2, col = c("#1f78b4", "#b2570b"),
        xlab = "Year", ylab = expression("Regional mean biomass (g m"^-2*")"))
legend("right", c("Pelagic predators", "Benthic detritivores"),
       col = c("#1f78b4", "#b2570b"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
```

And the size spectra the model produces in a productive (northern) versus a
cooler (southern) cell:

```{r fig.height = 4}
ok <- which(vapply(res$spec, is.list, logical(1)))
iN <- ok[which.max(ce$lat[ok])]; iS <- ok[which.min(ce$lat[ok])]
sN <- res$spec[[iN]]; sS <- res$spec[[iS]]
plot(sN$m/LN10, log10(pmax(sN$U, 1e-30)), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#1f78b4", ylim = c(-30, 5),
     xlab = expression(log[10]~"body mass (g)"), ylab = expression(log[10]~"abundance density"))
lines(sN$m/LN10, log10(pmax(sN$V, 1e-30)), lwd = 2, col = "#b2570b")
lines(sS$m/LN10, log10(pmax(sS$U, 1e-30)), lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "#1f78b4")
lines(sS$m/LN10, log10(pmax(sS$V, 1e-30)), lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "#b2570b")
legend("topright", c("pelagic (north)", "benthic (north)", "pelagic (south)", "benthic (south)"),
       col = c("#1f78b4", "#b2570b", "#1f78b4", "#b2570b"), lty = c(1, 1, 2, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
```

## 5. Adding fishing and calibrating to catch

The run above is unfished. To make it a *calibrated* regional model we add two more
FishMIP inputs — both downloadable per region from the
[FishMIP Input Explorer](https://fishmip.global-ecosystem-model.cloud.edu.au/shiny/FishMIP_Input_Explorer/):

* **fishing effort** (nominal effort by year), which drives fishing pressure, and
* **observed catch** (by functional group), the calibration target.

Effort is redistributed across cells each year by a **spatial-gravity** model
(more effort where accessible, high-biomass cells are), fishing is applied to size
classes above ~30 cm (separately for pelagic vs benthic/demersal groups mapped from
the catch functional groups), and the two catchabilities `q_pel`, `q_ben` are fitted
so aggregated modelled catch matches the observed series. Because Kerguelen has no
0-D anchor, we calibrate **directly on the grid** (spin cached once, then BOBYQA on
`log10(q)` with each objective evaluation running the fished transient). That step is
slow (many transients), so it is shown here but not run — we load its shipped result:

```{r eval = FALSE}
# Gridded-native q calibration (sketch; minutes-to-hours depending on region size):
#   spin unfished (cache) -> for each candidate (q_pel, q_ben):
#     transient 1961-2010 with annual gravity redistribution of FishMIP effort,
#     aggregate per-cell catch to a regional density series,
#     objective = wlogmse(agg_pel, obs_pel) + wlogmse(agg_ben, obs_ben)
#   BOBYQA over log10(q); observed catch split pelagic/benthic by functional group.
```

```{r fig.height = 4}
cal <- readRDS(ex("kerguelen_calib.rds"))
c(q_pel = cal$qg[1], q_ben = cal$qg[2])                       # fitted catchabilities
c(cor_pelagic = cal$corr_pel, cor_benthic = cal$corr_ben)    # modelled-vs-observed catch correlation

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4.2, 3, 1))
y <- cal$yrs; pos <- function(x) pmax(x, 1e-9)
yl <- range(c(cal$pel, cal$ben, cal$obs_pel, cal$obs_ben)[c(cal$pel, cal$ben, cal$obs_pel, cal$obs_ben) > 0])
plot(y, pos(cal$obs_pel), pch = 16, col = "#1f78b4", log = "y", ylim = yl,
     xlab = "Year", ylab = expression("Catch density (g m"^-2*" yr"^-1*")"), main = "Modelled vs observed catch")
points(y, pos(cal$obs_ben), pch = 16, col = "#b2570b")
lines(y, pos(cal$pel), col = "#1f78b4", lwd = 2); lines(y, pos(cal$ben), col = "#b2570b", lwd = 2)
legend("bottomright", c("pelagic obs", "pelagic model", "benthic obs", "benthic model"),
       pch = c(16, NA, 16, NA), lty = c(NA, 1, NA, 1), lwd = 2,
       col = c("#1f78b4", "#1f78b4", "#b2570b", "#b2570b"), bty = "n", cex = 0.75)

fc <- readRDS(ex("kerguelen_fished_cells.rds"))               # per-cell fished result
pal <- hcl.colors(64, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE)
plot(fc$lon, fc$lat, pch = 15, cex = 2.1, col = pal[as.integer(cut(log10(pos(fc$catch_tot)), 64))],
     xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude", main = "Modelled catch (2001-2010)")
points(c(69.2, 73.5), c(-49.3, -53.1), pch = 17)
```

The temporal fit is good in both groups (correlation ≈ 0.77 pelagic, 0.82 benthic):
the model reproduces the catch ramp-up and effort-driven variability, and catch
concentrates over the productive northern plateau where effort and biomass are
highest. Two honest limitations for this region: `q_ben` sits at its upper bound —
the model under-produces the large-bodied benthic (toothfish) catch *level* even at
maximum benthic catchability — and pelagic catch runs somewhat high. Both reflect
that a longline/deep-demersal fishery stresses the size-selective assumptions of a
generic size-spectrum model, not a data problem.

## 6. The whole region as one grid

So far every cell has been its own model run. The same region can instead be run
as **one two-dimensional grid**, with every input varying from cell to cell. With
movement switched off, each cell of the grid should then behave exactly like its
own single-cell run — a useful check before movement between cells is switched
on.

For this the inputs are handed to the model as **arrays** held in memory, indexed
`[x, y, month]`, rather than written to text files. Here we build them from the
bundled forcing table; when the forcing comes as NetCDF, `terra::rast()` followed
by `as.array()` gives the same arrays.

```{r}
lons <- sort(unique(cells$lon)); lats <- sort(unique(cells$lat))
ix   <- cbind(match(forc$lon, lons), match(forc$lat, lats), (forc$year - min(forc$year)) * 12 + forc$month)
arr  <- function(v) { a <- array(NA_real_, c(length(lons), length(lats), nmo)); a[ix] <- forc[[v]]; a }
Aint <- arr("intercept"); Aslp <- arr("slope"); Atex <- arr("texp"); Atob <- arr("tob"); Aexp <- arr("export")
depth <- matrix(NA_real_, length(lons), length(lats))
depth[cbind(match(cells$lon, lons), match(cells$lat, lats))] <- cells$depth
dim(Aint)                                                      # lon x lat x month
```

One function then runs either the whole grid or a single cell, depending only on
the arrays it is given. The plankton spectrum goes in as intercept and slope
arrays (`Setup.ts()`), temperature, export and depth as forcing arrays
(`Setup.Forcing()`), the depth-dependent benthic feeding preference as a per-cell
parameter (`Setup.CellParams()`), the starting spectra with `Setup.ts(initial = )`,
and the output comes back as arrays (`output = "arrays"`). With every input
held in memory and the output returned as arrays, the run reads and writes no
files; the record of its parameters comes back in the output object. The
functions that take arrays return the object they were given, which must be
assigned.
Fishing is optional and is used in the next section.

```{r eval = FALSE}
run_dbpm <- function(int, slp, tex, tob, exp, depth, nyr = 25, layer = NULL, fishing = NULL,
                     spacing = c(1, 1), prey = 0, pred = 0, comp = 0) {
  wd <- tempfile("dbpm"); dir.create(wd); old <- setwd(wd)
  on.exit({ setwd(old); unlink(wd, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE) }, add = TRUE)
  nx <- nrow(depth); ny <- ncol(depth); as_grid <- nx * ny > 1
  run  <- Setup.Run("R", 1, 1, if (as_grid) 2 else 0, TRUE, 1)
  grid <- if (as_grid) Setup.Grid(run, tmax = nyr, tstep = 1/48, toutstep = 0.5,
                                  xmin = 0, xmax = (nx - 1) * spacing[1], xstep = spacing[1], xoutstep = spacing[1],
                                  ymin = 0, ymax = (ny - 1) * spacing[2], ystep = spacing[2], youtstep = spacing[2])
          else Setup.Grid(run, tmax = nyr, tstep = 1/48, toutstep = 0.5)
  # the forcing layer each model time point uses: by default the supplied months repeat every year
  if (is.null(layer)) layer <- (floor(seq(0, nyr, 1/48) * 12) %% dim(int)[3]) + 1

  pl <- Setup.Plankton(run, filename = "plankton", ts_flag = TRUE)
  pl <- Setup.ts(pl, run, grid, intercept = 10^int / LN10, slope = slp, layer = layer)
  fo <- Setup.Forcing(run, grid, pel_tempeff = te(tex), ben_tempeff = te(tob),
                      sinking_rate = pmax(exp, 0), depth = pmin(depth, 200), layer = layer)
  fished <- !is.null(fishing)

  pe <- Setup.Pelagic(run, filename = "fish", mmin = -3*LN10, mmat = 2*LN10, mmax = 6*LN10,
                      alpha = params$metabolic_req_pred, A = 64*ascl, mu_0 = params$natural_mort*mu0s,
                      K_pla = Kp, R_pla = Rp, Ex_pla = Ep, K_pel = Kp, R_pel = Rp, Ex_pel = Ep,
                      K_ben = Kl, R_ben = Rl, Ex_ben = El, rep_method = 2, fishing_flag = fished,
                      prey = prey, pred = pred, comp = comp, initial_flag = TRUE, imm_frac = imm)
  be <- Setup.Benthic(run, filename = "benthos", mmin = -3*LN10, mmat = 1*LN10, mmax = 4*LN10,
                      alpha = params$metabolic_req_detritivore, A = 6.4*ascl, mu_0 = params$natural_mort*mu0s,
                      K_det = Kl, R_det = Rl, Ex_det = El, rep_method = 2, fishing_flag = fished,
                      initial_flag = TRUE)
  de <- Setup.Detritus(run, filename = "detritus")
  gv <- NULL
  if (fished) {                                                             # fishing mortality, held in memory
    pe <- Setup.fishing(pe, run, grid, rate = fishing$pel, min_size = fishing$min_size, layer = fishing$layer)
    be <- Setup.fishing(be, run, grid, rate = fishing$ben, min_size = fishing$min_size, layer = fishing$layer)
    if (!is.null(fishing$access))                                           # effort placed by gravity, updated every year
      gv <- Setup.Gravity(run, grid, access = fishing$access, pelagic_thickness = pmin(depth, 200),
                          benthic_thickness = 20, update = 1)
  }
  Setup.CellParams(pe, run, grid, pref_ben = 0.8 * exp(-depth / 1500))      # per-cell benthic preference
  start <- function(sp) {                                                   # the same starting spectrum in every cell
    m <- seq(sp@mmin, sp@mmax, length.out = round((sp@mmax - sp@mmin) / grid@mstep) + 1)
    matrix(sp@u_0 * exp(sp@lambda * m), nrow = 1)
  }
  Setup.ts(pe, run, grid, mat = start(pe)); Setup.ts(be, run, grid, mat = start(be))

  out <- NULL
  invisible(utils::capture.output(
    out <- SizeSpectrum(run, grid, pl, pe, be, de, forcing = fo, gravity = gv, output = "arrays",
                        variables = c("catch", "fishing"))))
  # sum over size classes and convert to per-area: pelagic over the top 200 m, benthic over a 20 m layer.
  # Abundance is weighted by body mass to give biomass; catch is already in biomass per size class.
  dm <- diff(out$m)[1]; last <- length(out$t)
  per_area <- function(a, wt, thick) apply(a, c(1, 2, 4), function(u) sum(u * wt)) * as.vector(thick)   # [x, y, time]
  res <- list(BU = per_area(out$abundance$fish, exp(out$m) * dm, pmin(depth, 200))[, , last, drop = FALSE][, , 1],
              BV = per_area(out$abundance$benthos, exp(out$m) * dm, 20)[, , last, drop = FALSE][, , 1])
  if (fished) {                                                             # catch rate at the middle of each year
    mid <- abs(out$t %% 1 - 0.5) < 1e-6
    res$catch <- list(pel = per_area(out$catch$fish, dm, pmin(depth, 200))[, , mid, drop = FALSE],
                      ben = per_area(out$catch$benthos, dm, 20)[, , mid, drop = FALSE])
    Fpel <- out$fishing$fish[, , length(out$m), mid, drop = FALSE]          # fishing mortality of the largest fish,
    dim(Fpel) <- dim(Fpel)[c(1, 2, 4)]                                      # as each cell's share of the grid total
    res$share <- sweep(Fpel, 3, pmax(apply(Fpel, 3, sum), 1e-300), "/")
  }
  res
}
```

Running it once with the full arrays gives the grid; running it for each cell in
turn, with that cell's slice of the same arrays, gives the single-cell runs. Both
spin up for 25 years on the first year of forcing, with movement off.

```{r eval = FALSE}
mo <- 1:12
grid_run <- run_dbpm(Aint[, , mo], Aslp[, , mo], Atex[, , mo], Atob[, , mo], Aexp[, , mo], depth)

one <- function(a, k, l) a[k, l, mo, drop = FALSE]             # a single cell keeps its [1, 1, month] shape
cell_runs <- list(BU = depth * NA, BV = depth * NA)
for (k in seq_along(lons)) for (l in seq_along(lats)) {
  r <- run_dbpm(one(Aint, k, l), one(Aslp, k, l), one(Atex, k, l), one(Atob, k, l), one(Aexp, k, l),
                depth[k, l, drop = FALSE])
  cell_runs$BU[k, l] <- r$BU; cell_runs$BV[k, l] <- r$BV
}
```

The shipped result of exactly these two chunks shows that the grid reproduces the
84 single-cell runs:

```{r fig.height = 4}
cmp <- readRDS(ex("kerguelen_grid_vs_cells.rds"))
c(pelagic = max(abs(cmp$grid$BU / cmp$cells$BU - 1)),          # largest relative difference in any cell
  benthic = max(abs(cmp$grid$BV / cmp$cells$BV - 1)))

par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
pal <- hcl.colors(64, "YlGnBu", rev = TRUE); zl <- range(cmp$cells$BU, cmp$grid$BU)
image(cmp$lon, cmp$lat, cmp$cells$BU, col = pal, zlim = zl, xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude",
      main = "Pelagic: 84 single-cell runs")
image(cmp$lon, cmp$lat, cmp$grid$BU, col = pal, zlim = zl, xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude",
      main = "Pelagic: one grid run")
plot(c(cmp$cells$BU, cmp$cells$BV), c(cmp$grid$BU, cmp$grid$BV), log = "xy", pch = 16,
     col = rep(c("#1f78b4", "#b2570b"), each = length(cmp$cells$BU)),
     xlab = "Single-cell runs", ylab = "Grid run", main = "Every cell, both groups")
abline(0, 1, col = "grey50")
```

Because the grid and the single-cell runs agree, differences that appear once
movement is switched on (`prey`, `pred` and `comp` in `run_dbpm()`) can be put
down to movement itself; section 8 does that. The output object can be saved with
`Write.NetCDF()`.

## 7. Fishing on the grid

Fishing on the grid has two parts. How much fishing there is changes through
*time*, and is forced here by the regional effort series. Where it falls in
*space* can be set in two ways: a **fixed share** of effort per cell, or a
**gravity** rule that moves effort towards the cells with the most accessible
catch as the run goes. Closed areas work with either.

### A fixed share of effort per cell

With a fixed share, fishing mortality in a cell and year is

> catchability × regional effort that year × number of cells × that cell's share of effort,

applied to all sizes above the minimum fished size. Here the share per cell is the
mean share over 2001--2010 from the calibrated run (shipped with the package), and
the catchabilities and minimum size are those of section 5. The rates go to the
model as `[x, y, layer]` arrays through `Setup.fishing()`, with one layer for the
unfished spin-up and one per year.

```{r}
cal <- readRDS(ex("kerguelen_calib.rds")); fc <- readRDS(ex("kerguelen_fished_cells.rds"))
share <- depth * NA                                            # share of effort per cell, [lon, lat]
share[cbind(match(fc$lon, lons), match(fc$lat, lats))] <- fc$eff / sum(fc$eff)
effort <- cal$Etot[as.character(cal$yrs)]                      # regional effort by year (1 = the peak year)
spin <- 25; nyear <- length(cal$yrs)

# fishing mortality [lon, lat, layer]: layer 1 is the unfished spin-up, then one layer per year
frate <- function(q) array(c(share * 0, outer(as.vector(share), q * length(share) * effort)), c(dim(share), nyear + 1))
tt    <- seq(0, spin + nyear, 1/48)                            # model time points (years)
fishing <- list(pel = frate(cal$qg[1]), ben = frate(cal$qg[2]), min_size = cal$UWLO * LN10,
                layer = ifelse(tt < spin, 1, pmin(floor(tt - spin + 1e-9), nyear - 1) + 2))
# the forcing month used at each time point: the first year repeats during the spin-up, then 1961-2010
months <- ifelse(tt < spin, (floor(tt * 12 + 1e-9) %% 12) + 1, pmin(floor((tt - spin) * 12 + 1e-9), nmo - 1) + 1)
round(range(fishing$pel[, , which.max(effort) + 1]), 4)        # pelagic fishing mortality across cells, peak year
```

The fished run uses the same function as before, once for the whole grid and once
per cell, now with the full monthly forcing and the fishing arrays:

```{r eval = FALSE}
fished_grid <- run_dbpm(Aint, Aslp, Atex, Atob, Aexp, depth, nyr = spin + nyear, layer = months, fishing = fishing)

cell <- function(a, k, l) a[k, l, , drop = FALSE]              # one cell, all layers
fished_cells <- list(pel = array(NA, c(dim(depth), nyear)), ben = array(NA, c(dim(depth), nyear)))
for (k in seq_along(lons)) for (l in seq_along(lats)) {
  r <- run_dbpm(cell(Aint, k, l), cell(Aslp, k, l), cell(Atex, k, l), cell(Atob, k, l), cell(Aexp, k, l),
                depth[k, l, drop = FALSE], nyr = spin + nyear, layer = months,
                fishing = list(pel = cell(fishing$pel, k, l), ben = cell(fishing$ben, k, l),
                               min_size = fishing$min_size, layer = fishing$layer))
  fished_cells$pel[k, l, ] <- r$catch$pel[1, 1, spin + seq_len(nyear)]
  fished_cells$ben[k, l, ] <- r$catch$ben[1, 1, spin + seq_len(nyear)]
}
catch_grid <- lapply(fished_grid$catch, function(a) a[, , spin + seq_len(nyear)])   # [lon, lat, year], g m^-2 yr^-1

# summarise: regional series (cells weighted by area), mean catch per cell for 2001-2010, grid vs single cells
wt  <- outer(rep(1, length(lons)), cos(lats * pi / 180))
reg <- function(a) apply(a, 3, function(z) sum(z * wt) / sum(wt))
rel <- function(g, s) { ok <- s > 1e-12 * max(s); max(abs(g[ok] / s[ok] - 1)) }
recent <- cal$yrs >= 2001
fg <- list(lon = lons, lat = lats, year = cal$yrs, pel = reg(catch_grid$pel), ben = reg(catch_grid$ben),
           cell_pel = apply(catch_grid$pel[, , recent], c(1, 2), mean), cell_ben = apply(catch_grid$ben[, , recent], c(1, 2), mean),
           agreement = c(pelagic = rel(catch_grid$pel, fished_cells$pel), benthic = rel(catch_grid$ben, fished_cells$ben)))
```

As for the unfished run, the grid and the single cells agree, and the forced run
gives a regional catch series and a map of where the catch is taken. The shipped
result of the chunks above:

```{r fig.height = 4}
fg <- readRDS(ex("kerguelen_fished_grid.rds"))
fg$agreement                                                   # largest relative difference, grid vs single cells

par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4.2, 3, 1))
pos <- function(x) pmax(x, 1e-9)
for (g in c("pel", "ben")) {
  obs <- cal[[paste0("obs_", g)]]; v <- c(obs, cal[[g]], fg[[g]]); yl <- range(v[v > 0])
  plot(fg$year, pos(obs), pch = 16, col = "grey40", log = "y", ylim = yl, xlab = "Year",
       ylab = expression("Catch (g m"^-2*" yr"^-1*")"), main = if (g == "pel") "Pelagic catch" else "Benthic catch")
  lines(fg$year, pos(cal[[g]]), lwd = 2, col = "#1f78b4"); lines(fg$year, pos(fg[[g]]), lwd = 2, col = "#d95f02")
  if (g == "pel") legend("bottomright", c("observed", "gravity (section 5)", "forced, fixed share"), pch = c(16, NA, NA),
                         lty = c(NA, 1, 1), lwd = 2, col = c("grey40", "#1f78b4", "#d95f02"), bty = "n", cex = 0.75)
}
image(fg$lon, fg$lat, log10(pos(fg$cell_pel + fg$cell_ben)), col = hcl.colors(64, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE),
      xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude", main = "Catch 2001-2010 (log10)")
```

The forced run follows the same effort series as the calibrated one but does not
match it exactly: with a fixed share, effort cannot follow the fish as they are
depleted. Because fishing is just an array, other spatial patterns are one line
away; a uniform share is `share[] <- 1 / length(share)`.

### Effort that follows the fish (gravity)

With `Setup.Gravity()` the model places the effort itself. The rate given to
`Setup.fishing()` is then the fishing mortality when effort is spread evenly,
catchability × regional effort that year, the same in every cell. Each cell's
share of effort is proportional to its accessibility times the catch that rate
would take there, and is updated every year from the current biomass. This is the
rule the calibrated run of section 5 used, there applied between yearly restarts
of the single-cell runs and here inside one grid run. Accessibility falls with
depth and with distance from shore:

```{r}
shore <- depth * NA
shore[cbind(match(cells$lon, lons), match(cells$lat, lats))] <- cells$shore_km
access <- exp(-depth / 800) * exp(-shore / 150)                # [lon, lat], between 0 and 1
# one rate per layer, the same in every cell: the unfished spin-up, then catchability x effort each year
gravity <- list(pel = c(0, cal$qg[1] * effort), ben = c(0, cal$qg[2] * effort),
                min_size = fishing$min_size, layer = fishing$layer, access = access)
```

### Closed areas

A marine protected area is a mask that multiplies the fishing rate: `[lon, lat]`
if it does not change, `[lon, lat, layer]` if it starts or ends during the run.
Such masks usually come as NetCDF, which reads straight into an array of that
shape with `ncdf4::ncvar_get()`, or with `terra::rast()` followed by
`as.array()`. Here we close a block of six cells on the southern bank from 2003
onwards. It is an illustration, not the boundary of a real reserve.

```{r}
mpa <- array(0, c(dim(depth), nyear + 1))                      # [lon, lat, layer], 1 = closed to fishing
mpa[lons > 72 & lons < 75, lats > -53 & lats < -51, c(FALSE, cal$yrs >= 2003)] <- 1
closed <- gravity                                              # the same fishing, with the closure
closed$pel <- sweep(1 - mpa, 3, gravity$pel, "*"); closed$ben <- sweep(1 - mpa, 3, gravity$ben, "*")
```

With gravity, effort that would have gone to a closed cell goes to the open cells
from the moment the closure starts; with a fixed share, setting the rate to zero
simply removes it.

```{r eval = FALSE}
full <- function(f, ...) run_dbpm(Aint, Aslp, Atex, Atob, Aexp, depth, nyr = spin + nyear, layer = months, fishing = f, ...)
summarise <- function(r, yrs = recent) {                       # regional series, and catch and effort share per cell
  cp <- r$catch$pel[, , spin + seq_len(nyear)]; cb <- r$catch$ben[, , spin + seq_len(nyear)]
  list(pel = reg(cp), ben = reg(cb), cell = apply((cp + cb)[, , yrs], c(1, 2), mean),
       share = apply(r$share[, , spin + seq_len(nyear)][, , yrs], c(1, 2), mean))
}
after <- cal$yrs >= 2004
with_gravity <- full(gravity); with_closure <- full(closed)
fg$gravity <- summarise(with_gravity)
fg$mpa <- c(summarise(with_closure, after),
            list(mask = mpa[, , nyear + 1], from = 2003, open_share = summarise(with_gravity, after)$share))
```

```{r fig.height = 4}
recent <- fg$year >= 2001
rbind("section 5 (single cells, yearly restarts)" = c(pelagic = mean(cal$pel[recent]), benthic = mean(cal$ben[recent])),
      "one grid, gravity"     = c(mean(fg$gravity$pel[recent]), mean(fg$gravity$ben[recent])),
      "one grid, fixed share" = c(mean(fg$pel[recent]), mean(fg$ben[recent])))      # catch 2001-2010, g m^-2 yr^-1

par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4.2, 3, 1))
plot(fg$year, pos(cal$pel), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#1f78b4", log = "y", ylim = c(1e-4, 1), xlim = c(1985, 2010),
     xlab = "Year", ylab = expression("Pelagic catch (g m"^-2*" yr"^-1*")"), main = "Gravity on the grid")
lines(fg$year, pos(fg$gravity$pel), lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "#d95f02"); lines(fg$year, pos(fg$mpa$pel), lwd = 2, col = "#1b9e77")
abline(v = fg$mpa$from, col = "grey60", lty = 3)
legend("bottomright", c("section 5", "one grid", "one grid, closure from 2003"), lty = c(1, 2, 1), lwd = 2,
       col = c("#1f78b4", "#d95f02", "#1b9e77"), bty = "n", cex = 0.75)
shpal <- hcl.colors(64, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE); zl <- c(0, max(fg$mpa$share, fg$mpa$open_share))
box_mpa <- function() {                                        # outline of the closed block
  k <- which(fg$mpa$mask == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
  rect(min(fg$lon[k[, 1]]) - 0.5, min(fg$lat[k[, 2]]) - 0.5, max(fg$lon[k[, 1]]) + 0.5, max(fg$lat[k[, 2]]) + 0.5, lwd = 2)
}
image(fg$lon, fg$lat, fg$mpa$open_share, col = shpal, zlim = zl, xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude",
      main = "Share of effort 2004-2010"); box_mpa()
image(fg$lon, fg$lat, fg$mpa$share, col = shpal, zlim = zl, xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude",
      main = "... with the closure"); box_mpa()
```

Run as one grid, gravity gives nearly the same catch as the calibrated run of
section 5, and puts the effort in the same cells. With the closure, the effort
leaves the outlined cells and concentrates on the northern shelf.

## 8. Movement between cells

Everything so far has had movement switched off, so each cell kept its own fish.
Movement needs the grid spacing as a distance, because its coefficients are in
distance squared per year. `run_dbpm()` takes the spacing as an argument; in
metres, with the east--west step taken at the middle latitude:

```{r}
dy <- 111200; dx <- round(dy * cos(mean(lats) * pi / 180))     # metres per degree of latitude and of longitude
K  <- dy^2                                                     # one squared degree of latitude, in m^2
c(dx = dx, dy = dy)
```

Two kinds of movement are used here: fish move towards cells where they grow
faster (`prey`), and spread out by diffusion (`comp`). Both coefficients are set
to `0.2 * K`, an illustrative value rather than an estimate. Avoidance of
predators (`pred`) is left off; on its own it is unstable, and `Setup.Pelagic()`
warns if it is used without diffusion (see the *spatial-movement* vignette).

```{r eval = FALSE}
still <- run_dbpm(Aint[, , mo], Aslp[, , mo], Atex[, , mo], Atob[, , mo], Aexp[, , mo], depth, spacing = c(dx, dy))
moved <- run_dbpm(Aint[, , mo], Aslp[, , mo], Atex[, , mo], Atob[, , mo], Aexp[, , mo], depth, spacing = c(dx, dy),
                  prey = 0.2 * K, comp = 0.2 * K)
fished_moved <- summarise(full(gravity, spacing = c(dx, dy), prey = 0.2 * K, comp = 0.2 * K))
mv <- list(lon = lons, lat = lats, still = still[c("BU", "BV")], moved = moved[c("BU", "BV")],
           pel = fished_moved$pel, ben = fished_moved$ben, share = fished_moved$share)
```

```{r fig.height = 4}
mv <- readRDS(ex("kerguelen_grid_movement.rds"))
rbind(still = range(mv$still$BU), moved = range(mv$moved$BU))  # pelagic biomass across cells, g m^-2

par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4.2, 3, 1))
zl <- range(mv$still$BU, mv$moved$BU)
image(mv$lon, mv$lat, mv$still$BU, col = pal, zlim = zl, xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude", main = "Pelagic: movement off")
image(mv$lon, mv$lat, mv$moved$BU, col = pal, zlim = zl, xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude", main = "Pelagic: movement on")
plot(fg$year, pos(fg$gravity$pel), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#d95f02", log = "y", ylim = c(1e-4, 1), xlim = c(1985, 2010),
     xlab = "Year", ylab = expression("Pelagic catch (g m"^-2*" yr"^-1*")"), main = "Fished with gravity")
lines(fg$year, pos(mv$pel), lwd = 2, col = "#7570b3")
legend("bottomright", c("movement off", "movement on"), lty = 1, lwd = 2, col = c("#d95f02", "#7570b3"), bty = "n", cex = 0.75)
```

The run is stable with movement on, and movement evens out the biomass between
neighbouring cells. It also lowers the catch several-fold at the same
catchability. The movement coefficients grow with body size, so the large fish
that are fished mix across the whole region and no longer build up in the few
accessible cells where the effort is. Catchabilities calibrated with movement off
therefore do not carry over: with movement on, the calibration of section 5 has
to be repeated.

## Going further

* **The full gridded workflow.** For the pre-calibrated large regions the pipeline
  also does per-cell forcing → LME-centering → gridded `q` calibration → fished run;
  see the package's gridded workflow (`GRIDDED_WORKFLOW.md`).
* **Another region.** Swap in any FishMIP regional boundary from
  [Fish-MIP/FishMIP_regions](https://github.com/Fish-MIP/FishMIP_regions), pull its
  forcing, effort and catch from the
  [FishMIP Input Explorer](https://fishmip.global-ecosystem-model.cloud.edu.au/shiny/FishMIP_Input_Explorer/),
  and reuse exactly the `run_cell()` loop and the calibration sketch above.
